# cancel of a job never submitted whose upload ID is known asks the
# server to delete that upload, once. The reply means the server marked
# it for deletion; afterwards nothing is sent again. A submitted job's
# upload is the job's and is never cleaned up.

skygo-ec2 start -config $CONFIG -state $STATE -credentials $CREDS -interval 0
code 0

# The first chunk's reply is lost: the upload ID is known, nothing was
# submitted.
lose WriteArtifactChunk 1
! job run -job $WORK/up -task $WORK/task.json -workdir $WORK/src
code 1
stdout '"upload": "open"'
stdout '"submit": "none"'
opens 1

job cancel -job $WORK/up
code 0
stdout '"state": "NEVER_SUBMITTED"'
stdout '"cleanup": "delivered"'
stdout '"upload_id": "[0-9a-f]{32}"'
calls CancelArtifactUpload 1
opens 2

# A delivered cleanup needs no VM, session or request.
ec2mark
job cancel -job $WORK/up
code 0
stdout '"cleanup": "delivered"'
ec2since 0
opens 2
calls CancelArtifactUpload 1
accepted BeginArtifactUpload 1
calls SubmitWorkspaceJob 0
jobs 0

# The twin: a submitted job ended; cancel sends nothing and cleans
# nothing up.
job run -job $WORK/done -task $WORK/task.json -workdir $WORK/src -poll 100ms
code 0
! job cancel -job $WORK/done
code 4
stdout '"state": "SUCCEEDED"'
! stdout '"cleanup"'
calls CancelArtifactUpload 1
calls CancelJob 0
jobs 1

mutations 1

-- task.json --
{"argv":["/bin/true"],"timeoutSeconds":"60"}
-- src/input.txt --
input
